literal: Winter, tenth month: moved to Yunzhong, attacked the Gaoche Douchen division at Langshan, and defeated them.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he moved the court to Yunzhong, struck the Gaoche Douchen at Langshan, and broke them.

literal: Eleventh month: Kuhan, grandee of the Hexi tribe, led his tribe to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kuhan, chieftain of the Hexi, brought his people in submission.

literal: Twelfth month: Qudijian, grandee of the Hetulin tribe, led his tribe to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Qudijian, chieftain of the Hetulin, led his clan to submit.

literal: The emperor returned and halted at Baimo.
idiomatic: The emperor withdrew and encamped at Baimo.

literal: Year 6, spring, second month: visited Niudichuan.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, in the second month of spring, he went to Niudichuan.

literal: Third month: sent Jiuyuan Prince Yuan Yi, Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian, and others west to attack the Chufu tribe, greatly defeating them.
idiomatic: In the third month he sent Prince Yuan Yi of Jiuyuan and Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu west against the Chufu and routed them.

literal: Summer, fourth month: sacrificed to Heaven.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he offered sacrifice to Heaven.

literal: Sixth month: Murong Helin defeated He Ne at Chicheng.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Murong Helin defeated He Ne at Chicheng.

literal: The emperor led troops to rescue him; Helin withdrew and fled.
idiomatic: The emperor marched to his relief; Helin broke off and fled.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renshen: conducted martial exercises at Niuchuan, then on the march returned to Niudichuan.
idiomatic: On the renshen day of the seventh month of autumn he held a military review at Niuchuan, then returned to Niudichuan.

literal: Murong Chui detained Yuan Gu and demanded famous horses; the emperor refused.
idiomatic: Murong Chui held Yuan Gu hostage and demanded prized horses; the emperor refused.

literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to Murong Yong; Yong had his Grand Herald Murong Jun present a memorial urging assumption of the exalted title.
idiomatic: He then sent envoys to Murong Yong, who had his Grand Herald Murong Jun submit a memorial urging him to take the imperial title.

literal: That month, Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi out from Puyang Pass, invading as far as Heicheng.
idiomatic: That same month Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi through Puyang Pass to raid as far as Heicheng.

literal: Ninth month: the emperor raided Wuyuan and slaughtered it.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he stormed Wuyuan and put the city to the sword.

literal: Collected their stored grain and returned to Niudichuan.
idiomatic: He seized their granaries and withdrew to Niudichuan.

literal: North of Puyang Pass, erected a stele recording merit.
idiomatic: North of Puyang Pass he raised a stele to commemorate the victory.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuxu: northern campaign against the Rouran, pursued them, caught up south of the great desert below South Bed Mountain, greatly defeated them, distributed rewards to accompanying ministers each according to rank.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the tenth month of winter he marched north against the Rouran, pursued them to South Bed Mountain south of the great desert, crushed them, and rewarded his officers by rank.

literal: The eastern and western division leaders Pihouba and Wenheti, [5] beheaded the separate commander Wujiyu.
idiomatic: The chiefs of the eastern and western wings, Pihouba and Wenheti, [5] cut down the sub-commander Wujiyu.

literal: The matter is fully set out in the Rouran biography.
idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of the Rouran.

literal: Eleventh month, day wuchen: returned and visited Niudichuan.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the eleventh month he returned to Niudichuan.

literal: On day wuyin, Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to raid the southern frontier.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day Weichen sent Zhiligidi to attack the southern marches.

literal: On day jimao, the imperial carriage set out on campaign.
idiomatic: On the jimao day the emperor took the field in person.

literal: On day renwu, greatly defeated Zhiligidi's army south of Tieqi Mountain, capturing their weapons, baggage, and more than two hundred thousand cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: On the renwu day he shattered Zhiligidi's army south of Tieqi Mountain and seized arms, wagons, and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock.

literal: On day wuzi, crossed the river south from Jinyuan Ford at Wuyuan.
idiomatic: On the wuzi day he forded the Yellow River south from Jinyuan at Wuyuan.

literal: On day xinmao, halted at their residence Yueba City; Weichen father and son fled.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day he reached their stronghold at Yueba; Weichen and his son fled.

literal: On day renchen, ordered the generals to pursue and captured Zhiligidi.
idiomatic: On the renchen day he ordered his generals in pursuit and took Zhiligidi alive.

literal: Twelfth month: obtained Weichen's corpse, beheaded and displayed it, then destroyed them completely.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he recovered Weichen's body, had it beheaded and paraded, and extinguished his line.

literal: The account is in the biography of Weichen.
idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Weichen.

literal: Weichen's youngest son Qu Fu fled to the Xuegan tribe.
idiomatic: Weichen's youngest son Qu Fu escaped to the Xuegan tribe.

literal: [6] The imperial carriage halted at Salt Pool.
idiomatic: [6] The court encamped at Salt Pool.

literal: From the river southward, all tribes were pacified.
idiomatic: South of the river every tribe was brought to submission.

literal: Registered their treasures and livestock: more than three hundred thousand famous horses, more than four million cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: He inventoried their wealth and herds: over three hundred thousand fine horses and more than four million cattle and sheep.

literal: Distributed rewards to great ministers each according to rank.
idiomatic: He rewarded his chief ministers according to their stations.

literal: Took Weichen's sons, younger brothers, and clansmen young and old, more than five thousand persons, and killed them all.
idiomatic: More than five thousand of Weichen's kin, young and old, were seized and put to death.

literal: Shanhu chiefs Dafantui, Yeyiyu, and others led more than three thousand households to submit and were settled at Mayi.
idiomatic: Dafantui and Yeyiyu of the Shanhu, with more than three thousand households, submitted and were resettled at Mayi.

literal: That year, built Henan Palace.
idiomatic: That year he began the Henan Palace.

literal: Year 7, spring, first month: visited Mugen Mountain, then halted at Black Salt Pool.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, in the first month of spring, he went to Mugen Mountain and then encamped at Black Salt Pool.

literal: Feasted the host of ministers and received tribute envoys from various states.
idiomatic: He feasted his ministers and received envoys bearing tribute from the surrounding states.

literal: North to Meishui.
idiomatic: He continued north to Meishui.

literal: Third month, day jiazi: feasted ministers at the waterside, returned and visited Henan Palace.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month he banqueted his ministers on the riverbank, then returned to the Henan Palace.

literal: Western Qili grandee Maoxian rebelled and fled; sent southern grandee Zhangsun Song in pursuit and greatly defeated him.
idiomatic: Maoxian, chieftain of the western Qili, rose in revolt and fled; Zhangsun Song was sent in pursuit and routed him.

literal: Summer, fifth month: distributed horses, cattle, and sheep to officials each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he gave horses, cattle, and sheep to his officials according to rank.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: traveled to south of the desert, also built a patrol platform.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he toured south of the desert and built a patrol platform.

literal: Winter, twelfth month: Murong Yong sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Murong Yong sent envoys to court.

literal: That year, the imperial son Si was born.
idiomatic: That year the prince Si was born.

literal: Year 8, spring, first month: the emperor made a southern tour.
idiomatic: In the eighth year, in the first month of spring, the emperor toured the south.

literal: Second month: visited Goyang Plain, proceeded to Bailou.
idiomatic: In the second month he went to Goyang Plain and on to Bailou.

literal: Third month: the imperial carriage west to campaign against the Houlülin tribe.
idiomatic: In the third month the court marched west against the Houlülin.

literal: Source annotation [7].
idiomatic: Editorial note [7].

literal: Summer, fourth month: reached Kushui, greatly defeated them.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he reached Kushui and crushed them.

literal: Fifth month: returned and visited Bailou.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he returned to Bailou.

literal: Murong Chui attacked Murong Yong at Changzi.
idiomatic: Murong Chui besieged Murong Yong at Changzi.

literal: Sixth month: the imperial carriage made a northern tour.
idiomatic: In the sixth month the court toured the north.

literal: Yong came reporting urgency; sent Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian and General Yu Yue leading fifty thousand cavalry east across the river to rescue.
idiomatic: Yong sent word that he was hard pressed; the emperor dispatched Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu and General Yu Yue with fifty thousand horsemen east across the river to relieve him.

literal: Defeated Leiba division commander Liu Yao and others, relocated their tribes.
idiomatic: They defeated Liu Yao, chief of the Leiba division, and resettled his people.

literal: Yuan Qian and others therefore camped at Xiurong; Murong Chui then besieged Changzi.
idiomatic: Yuan Qian's force encamped at Xiurong while Murong Chui tightened the siege of Changzi.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage visited Xintan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court visited Xintan.

literal: On day gengyin, feasted ministers and again conducted martial exercises.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day he feasted his ministers and held another military review.

literal: Earlier, Weichen's son Qu Fu had fled to the Xuegan tribe; they were summoned to hand him over but did not.
idiomatic: Earlier Qu Fu, Weichen's son, had taken refuge with the Xuegan; when the court demanded his surrender, they refused.

literal: Eighth month: the emperor southern campaign against Xuegan chief Taxisifu at Sancheng; as it happened they had gone out earlier to attack Cao Fu; the emperor seized the vacancy and slaughtered their city, captured Taxisifu's sons and treasures, relocated the people and returned.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched south against Taxisifu of the Xuegan at Sancheng. Taxisifu had already led his men out against Cao Fu; the emperor struck the empty city, slaughtered it, seized his sons and treasure, resettled the people, and withdrew.

literal: Taxisifu heard of it, came but could not arrive in time, then fled to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: Taxisifu hurried back too late and fled to Yao Xing.

literal: Ninth month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to the Henan Palace.

literal: That year, Yao Chang died.
idiomatic: That year Yao Chang died.

literal: Year 9, spring, third month: the emperor made a northern tour.
idiomatic: In the ninth year, in the third month of spring, the emperor toured the north.

literal: Sent Dongping Prince Yuan Yi to garrison-farm in Wuyuan north of the river, reaching beyond Puyang Pass.
idiomatic: He set Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping to farm garrisons in Wuyuan north of the river, as far as beyond Puyang Pass.

literal: Summer, fifth month: farmed at Hedong.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he oversaw farming at Hedong.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he returned to the Henan Palace.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Rouran Shelun and others led their tribes west in flight.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Shelun of the Rouran led his tribes west in flight.

literal: The matter is fully set out in the Rouran biography.
idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of the Rouran.

literal: That year, Yao Chang's son Xing presumptuously established himself and killed Fu Deng.
idiomatic: That year Yao Chang's son Xing declared himself emperor in defiance of the court and killed Fu Deng.

literal: Murong Chui destroyed Yong.
idiomatic: Murong Chui overthrew Murong Yong.

literal: Year 10, spring, first month: Taxisifu from Chang'an returned to north of the ridges; west of Shang commandery all responded.
idiomatic: In the tenth year, in the first month of spring, Taxisifu returned from Chang'an to the country north of the ridges, and the region west of Shang commandery rose for him.

literal: Summer, fifth month: visited Salt Pool.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he went to Salt Pool.

literal: Sixth month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he returned to the Henan Palace.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Murong Chui sent his son Bao to raid Wuyuan, building boats to gather grain.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Chui sent his son Bao against Wuyuan to build boats and gather grain.

literal: The emperor sent Right Marshal Xu Qian to levy troops from Yao Xing.
idiomatic: The emperor sent the Right Marshal Xu Qian to raise troops from Yao Xing.

literal: Dongping Prince Yuan Yi moved to hold Shuofang.
idiomatic: Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping shifted his base to Shuofang.

literal: Eighth month: the emperor personally drilled troops at Henan.
idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor personally reviewed the army at Henan.

literal: Ninth month: advanced the army, built a platform by the river to announce the crossing, continuous banners along the river east and west for more than a thousand li.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he advanced, raised a platform on the riverbank to proclaim the crossing, and stretched his banners along the Yellow River for more than a thousand li.

literal: At that time, Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian with fifty thousand cavalry in the east to cut off their left; Yuan Yi fifty thousand cavalry north of the river to receive them from behind; Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun seventy thousand cavalry blocked the road through Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu lay in wait east of them with fifty thousand horse; Yuan Yi with fifty thousand blocked the north bank; Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang sealed the passes through Zhongshan with seventy thousand.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinwei: Bao burned the boats and fled by night.
idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the tenth month of winter Bao burned his fleet and stole away by night.

literal: Eleventh month, day jimao: the emperor advanced the army and crossed the river.
idiomatic: On the jimao day of the eleventh month the emperor crossed the river in force.

literal: On the evening of day yiyou, reached Canhe Marsh.
idiomatic: On the evening of the yiyou day he came to Canhe Marsh.

literal: On day bingxu, greatly defeated them.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day he won a crushing victory.

literal: The account is in the biography of Bao.
idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Murong Bao.

literal: Alive captured the Chenliu King Shao, Luyang King Wonu, Guilin Prince Daocheng, Jiyin Duke Yin Guo, Beidi King's heir Zhongkui, Anding King's heir Yang'er and below civil and military officers and generals numbering several thousand persons, armor and baggage, military supplies and miscellaneous goods reckoned at more than one hundred thousand.
idiomatic: He took alive the Chenliu king Shao, the Luyang king Wonu, the Guilin prince Daocheng, the Jiyin duke Yin Guo, the heir of the king of Beidi Zhongkui, the heir of the king of Anding Yang'er, and thousands of civil and military officers, with arms, wagons, and supplies in the tens of thousands.

literal: From among captives selected those of talent and learning — Jia Yi, Jia Gui, Chao Chong, and others — to join in counsel and planning, statutes and models of ancient practice.
idiomatic: From the prisoners he chose men of talent — Jia Yi, Jia Gui, Chao Chong, and others — to advise him on laws and precedent.

literal: Distributed rewards to great ministers, generals, and officers each according to rank.
idiomatic: He rewarded his ministers and commanders according to their merit.

literal: Twelfth month: returned and visited Shengle in Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.

literal: Summer, sixth month, day guiyou: sent General Wang Jian and three armies to attack Bao's Guangning administrator Liu Kangni, beheaded him, relocated his tribe.
idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the sixth month of summer he sent General Wang Jian with three columns against Liu Kangni, Bao's administrator of Guangning; Kangni was beheaded and his people resettled.

literal: Bao's Shanggu administrator Murong Pulins abandoned the commandery and fled.
idiomatic: Murong Pulins, Bao's administrator of Shanggu, abandoned his post and fled.

literal: On day dinghai, the Empress Dowager of the He clan died.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day the Empress Dowager He died.

literal: That month, buried the Xianming Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: That month the Xianming Empress Dowager was buried.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Left Marshal Xu Qian submitted a memorial urging the exalted title; the emperor first established Son of Heaven banners, entry and exit with imperial guard; thereupon changed the era name.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Xu Qian urged him to take the imperial title; the emperor first raised the imperial standard and traveled under guard, and proclaimed a new reign era.

literal: Eighth month, day gengyin: drilled troops at the eastern suburb.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the eighth month he reviewed the army at the eastern suburb.

literal: On day jihai, great campaign against Murong Bao; the emperor personally led the six armies, more than four hundred thousand, south from Mayi, crossing Juzhu Pass, banners and pennants continuous for more than two thousand li, drums beating as they advanced, civilian houses all shaking.
idiomatic: On the jihai day he launched a great campaign against Murong Bao. At the head of more than four hundred thousand men he marched south from Mayi over Juzhu Pass; his banners filled the road for two thousand li, the drums rolled forward, and houses trembled in his path.

literal: Separate order to General Feng Zhen and three armies from the eastern route to raid Youzhou, besiege Ji.
idiomatic: He also ordered General Feng Zhen with three columns to strike east, invest Youzhou, and besiege Ji.

literal: Ninth month, day wuwu: halted at Yangqu, ascended Western Mountain, overlooked Jinyang, ordered generals to lead cavalry in surrounding threat, then soon withdrew.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the ninth month he halted at Yangqu, climbed the western hills to look down on Jinyang, sent his generals to wheel cavalry about the city in feint, then withdrew.

literal: Bao's Bingzhou governor Liaoxi King Nong was greatly afraid, took wife and children, abandoned the city by night and fled east; Bingzhou pacified.
idiomatic: Murong Nong, Bao's governor of Bingzhou and king of Liaoxi, fled the city by night with his family; Bingzhou was pacified.

literal: First established the terrace departments, set all offices, enfeoffed marquises and dukes, generals, regional inspectors, and administrators; Secretariat gentlemen and below all used literary men.
idiomatic: He founded the central secretariat, appointed the full bureaucracy, enfeoffed nobles and generals and named inspectors and administrators, and staffed the Secretariat and lower offices with literati.
